item.title: Available Dashboards
item.description:
Available Dashboards#

The dashboards come in two families: those scoped to a Materialize environment (env-*), and those scoped to the platform underneath it (infra-*). The infra-* dashboards that watch the monitoring stack itself, rather than anything it collects, are filed in the Meta Observability folder. Each one below has its own download links and its own compatibility annotations.

If you install the dashboards charts, you don’t need to download anything. Each chart installs every dashboard it carries by default, and the Grafana Operator path keeps them in sync rather than importing a point-in-time copy. materialize-monitoring-dashboards carries the env-* dashboards, materialize-monitoring-dashboards-meta carries the dashboards in the Meta Observability folder, and materialize-monitoring-dashboards-infra carries the rest of the infra-* dashboards. Download them when you are putting them into a Grafana you run yourself; Importing Dashboards covers the ways to do that.

item.title: Datadog
item.description:
Datadog#

The Materialize Environment Overview, env-top, has a Datadog version. It holds the Grafana dashboard’s panels, apart from the differences listed on this page, under the same tabs, with a group for each Grafana row. The rest of the Grafana dashboards are tracked as DEP-115, on the Dashboards roadmap. On this page, “you” are an operator who sends Materialize metrics to Datadog.

Import the dashboard#

  1. Download the Datadog file from the env-top row of Available Dashboards.

  2. Create the dashboard through Datadog’s API, with an API key and an application key that has the dashboards_write permission:

    curl -X POST "https://api.DATADOG_SITE/api/v1/dashboard" \
 -H "DD-API-KEY: ${DD_API_KEY}" \
 -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: ${DD_APP_KEY}" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 --data @datadog-env-top.json

    Replace DATADOG_SITE with your Datadog site, such as datadoghq.com. If you manage Datadog with Terraform, pass the same file to the Datadog provider’s datadog_dashboard_json resource instead.

  3. Pick one environment in the environment variable, and the namespace it runs in in the namespace variable.
